name: Muangphe
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Muangphe: only Hsiu 2014 wordlist/classification noted on Glottolog; no phonology/grammar describing stress located

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2017. Mondzish lexical database (xlsx, 436 rows, 24 lects; col. B = Muangphe, Xinfazhai). Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.1249169
sources.note: Wordlist only; every Muangphe form carries Chao tone numerals, no stress marks, no notes column for Muangphe (Sources sheet: 'Hsiu, Andrew. 2013. Audio recordings').

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2018. Muangphe (Mondzish branch pages, 'Southeast Asian languages' site).https://sites.google.com/site/msealangs/mondzish-branch/muangphe
sources.note: Nothing; repeats Hsiu 2014 §2.2 (pre-velarized initials; pharyngeal consonants 'like Northern Qiang, Atayal, and Amis').

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. Muangphe audio word list (2013), 225 wav files; and (2012), 37 wav files. Zenodo.
sources.note: The only primary acoustic data on Muangphe in existence (single informant, Xinfazhai); an instrumental look could establish whether any non-tonal prominence exists, but no written statement will come out of it.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2014-2017. Survey of Highly Endangered Mondzish Languages in Yunnan, China. Experiment.com crowdfunding project page, doi:10.18258/4173 (the only Crossref hit for 'Mondzish'; Crossref 'Muangphe' = 0 hits)
sources.note: No phonological description; only mentions archaic kl- clusters in Kathu.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2014. Mondzish: a new branch of Lolo-Burmese. Presentation slides, IsCLL-14, Academia Sinica, 29 pp. Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.1127814
sources.note: Nothing; classification slides with tone-numeral wordlist items, autonym muaŋ⁵³ / muaŋ⁵⁵phe²¹, population 300 in Xinfazhai.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2014. Mondzish: a new subgroup of Lolo-Burmese. Preliminary draft for the 14th International Symposium on Chinese Languages and Linguistics (IsCLL-14), Academia Sinica, Taipei, 4-6 June 2014, 20 pp. (published in Proceedings of IsCLL-14, pp. 62-81). Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.1127814
sources.note: Nothing. Section 2.2 'Muangphe' (pp. 6-7) is sociolinguistic (villages, vitality, ethnonym Lai/Lairen) plus one phonological remark: 'Phonologically, Muangphe is characterized by the pre-velarization of many of its initials'. The Appendix (pp. 17-20) is a 92-item comparative wordlist with Chao tone numerals (e.g. muaŋ⁵⁵phe²¹, te³³e³³); no stress or accent is marked or discussed anywhere in the paper. a full-text search for stress/accent returns zero hits.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2013. New endangered Tibeto-Burman languages of southwestern China: Mondzish, Longjia, Pherbu, and others. Slides, ICSTLL 46, Dartmouth College, 8 Aug 2013, 24 pp. Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.1127796
sources.note: Nothing; first announcement of Muangphe (muɑŋ⁵⁵phɛ³³, ~300 speakers, Xinfazhai) with a few comparative items in tone numerals.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page muan1234 (Muangphe); Wikipedia 'Muangphe language' and 'Mondzish languages'
sources.note: Glottolog lists exactly one reference (Hsiu 2014) and no phonology/grammar; Wikipedia pages cite only Hsiu 2014, Hsiu 2018 web page, Lama 2012 and Edmondson 2003 and carry no phonology.

sources.citation: 李旭练 Li Xulian. 1999. 俫语研究 [A study of the Lai (Bolyu) language]. Beijing: 中央民族大学出版社.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Cited by Hsiu 2014 only for the Guangnan 'Lai 俫' village demographics (Table 3); it is a description of Austroasiatic Bolyu, not Muangphe, but it is the one Chinese work that mentions the Muangphe villages and might contain a wordlist or remark on their (Yi) speech.

sources.citation: 广南县志 / 文山壮族苗族自治州志 (Guangnan County Gazetteer; Wenshan Prefecture Gazetteer), ethnic/language chapters.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Chinese county/prefecture gazetteers sometimes carry a paragraph and a short wordlist on small unclassified Yi lects such as the Guangnan Lairen; unverified whether any covers Muangphe. CNKI not accessible).
